item.title: 'A second set of eyes': AI-supported breast cancer screening spots more cancers earlier, landmark trial finds
item.description: A clinical trial shows that AI-assisted mammography can detect more cases of dangerous cancer and reduce missed diagnoses.

item.title: Anglo-Saxon children discovered buried with warrior gear in UK — perhaps as a nod to 'the men these children might have become'
item.description: Archaeologists have discovered Anglo-Saxon children buried with a spear, shield and buckles, gear that's usually seen in warriors' graves.

item.title: Science history: 'Father of modern genetics' describes his experiments with pea plants — and proves that heredity is transmitted in discrete units — Feb. 8, 1865
item.description: Gregor Mendel described his experiments with pea plants and proved that genes are transmitted in discrete units, with certain fundamental laws of inheritance.

item.title: 'Maybe they're waiting for something that only happens thousands of years later': The hidden life 'sleeping' deep beneath Earth for millions of years
item.description: Deep inside Earth lies a hidden world of "intraterrestrials" that have been dormant for hundreds of thousands of years — what are they waiting to "wake up" for?

item.title: Did ancient Greeks let women compete in the Olympics?
item.description: The ancient Olympic games were crowded with male athletes, but were there opportunities for females to compete in sports?

item.title: Dramatic death of Comet C/2025 K1 (ATLAS) caught on camera — Space photo of the week
item.description: The Gemini North telescope snapped a spectacular view of Comet C/2025 K1 (ATLAS) breaking apart as it emerged from the other side of the sun in October.

item.title: Physicists push quantum boundaries by turning a superfluid into a supersolid — and back — for the first time
item.description: Physicists saw excitons, a type of quasiparticle, undergo a reversible phase transition from superfluid to supersolid for the first time, opening new doors for studying extreme states of matter.

item.title: Microbes in Iceland are hoarding nitrogen, and that's mucking up the nutrient cycle
item.description: A study in Iceland found that microbes are hoarding more nitrogen for themselves, altering nutrient cycling and leaving less for plants.

item.title: 'Night owls' may have worse heart health — but why?
item.description: Emerging evidence suggests that "night owls" are more likely to have poor heart health and a higher risk of heart attack or stroke than "morning larks." Why is that?

item.title: Paleo-Inuit people braved icy seas to reach remote Greenland islands 4,500 years ago, archaeologists discover
item.description: Archaeological remains on the Kitsissut islands off the coast of Greenland reveal that whole communities regularly journeyed across the dangerous Arctic waters.
